data.title: CleanSpark Completes $2.276 Billion 7.875% Notes to Fund Sandersville Facility
data.description:
CleanSpark completed a $2.276 billion private offering of 7.875% Senior Secured Notes, priced at 98.500% of par, to finance its Sandersville, Georgia data center project, reimburse prior equity contributions, and fund debt service reserves. The company’s subsidiary, CSDC Finance I, entered into an Indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company as trustee and collateral agent, setting interest, amortization, redemption, and covenant terms through 2031. The sale was executed under a purchase agreement with Morgan Stanley as representative of the initial purchasers under Rule 144A/Reg S. CleanSpark also provided a completion guarantee to ensure the project is finished on time if proceeds and available funds are insufficient.

data.title: Nasdaq gains 2% for the week driven by mid-week tech rally
data.description:
The Nasdaq Composite Index ended higher Friday following a  mid-week rally in tech stocks that pushed the index to new all-time highs. Major Wall Street indexes also closed higher as yields eased and oil dipped as attention remained on the Strait of Hormuz.

Nasdaq ended 0.48% higher at 27,068.72. It gained 2.1% for the week.

The move marked the first time the tech-heavy benchmark traded at a record since early summer, with semiconductor stocks leading the gains.

Gainers for the week ended September 25 were led by Astera Labs , which advanced 21%, adding to the rally. Datadog added more than 16%, logging the second-highest gains for the week.

Chip stocks including Qualcomm , Intel , Advanced Micro Devices , and Arm Holdings were among the top 10 gainers of the week.

Among the decliners, Paychex lost the most, declining nearly 13% for the week following its quarterly results, where management stopped short of raising its guidance.

data.title: CME cattle jump as low US supply outweighs slow processing
data.description:
By Tom Polansek

Live cattle and feeder cattle futures galloped higher on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange on Friday as concerns about limited US inventories overshadowed processing disruptions, analysts said.

The US Department of Agriculture highlighted low supplies a week ago by reporting that placements of cattle into US feedlots last month were the lowest August total in records dating to 1996.

CME December live cattle rose 1.050 cents to close at 222.150 cents per pound on Friday. October feeder cattle jumped 3.175 cents to close at 334.925 cents per pound.

Cattle slaughtering has declined this week as an immigration crackdown in southwestern Kansas has kept meatpacking workers away from beef plants. Shipments of thousands of cattle have been delayed, according to groups representing livestock producers.

ICE did not comment, though some traders said they worried disruptions could extend into next week.

"ICE’s targeting of these communities sows fear, instability, and chaos into the lives of those trying to make a living and feed our nation," said Milton Jones, president of the United Food and Commercial Workers International Union.

"These disruptions directly impact the safety of all workers and the supply of beef."

Meatpackers on Friday slaughtered an estimated 87,000 cattle, down 14% from a week earlier, according to the US Department of Agriculture.

In CME's lean hog market, December (LHZ26) futures slumped 0.450 cent to 69.025 cents per pound.

USDA, in a report issued after trading ended on Thursday, said the total US hog inventory was 74.3 million head as of September 1, down 1.5% from a year earlier. Analysts expected a decline of 0.8%, according to a Reuters poll.

After trading ended on Friday, USDA said stocks of frozen pork bellies on August 31 were down 35% from a month earlier and 1% from last year.

data.title: RegenLab Files for IPO
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

RegenLab filed for an initial public offering.

The regenerative medicine company plans to trade shares on Nasdaq under the ticker RGNA.

RegenLab was founded in Switzerland and is now U.S.-based. It operates three manufacturing sites and dedicated research and development and clinical teams in New Jersey, Paris and Monthey, Switzerland.

It maintains full control of the development and industrialization cycle.

The company has numerous products across different stages of regulatory approval in both the E.U. and U.S. That includes products in musculoskeletal regeneration, advanced wound care, medical aesthetics and dermatology, and women's health and urogynecology.

RegenLab didn't disclose the pricing or amount of shares it plans to offer.

data.title: Coca-Cola Taps Monster Executive as President of North American Unit
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

Coca-Cola named Rob Gehring as president of its North America operating unit.

Gehring will start Dec. 1 and succeed John Murphy, who has led the unit on an interim basis since Aug. 1. Murphy remains president and chief financial officer.

Gehring, 59, most recently served as chief executive of Monster Energy's Americas business, which he started in February.

He began his career at Coca-Cola in 1992 before moving up to president of Coca-Cola's Walmart global team in 2011. In 2016, he joined Hershey, where he served as chief sales officer.

In 2018, Gehring was appointed as chief operating officer, and later chief executive, of Swire Coca-Cola, where he led bottling operations.

data.title: Top News Today: U.S. Stocks Rise To End Volatile Week
data.description:
MARKET WRAPS

STOCKS: U.S. stocks recovered from a couple of down sessions as oil prices fell on hopes for progress toward an agreement between the U.S. and Iran to open the Strait of Hormuz.

TREASURYS: The bonds selloff cooled down as the oil rally paused, but yields still ended the week at multi-year highs.

FOREX: The U.S. dollar pulled back following four straight sessions of gains.

COMMODITIES: Oil prices fell as investors assessed prospects for U.S.-Iran diplomacy aimed at reopening the Strait of Hormuz while keeping a measure of caution given continued Houthi threats to Saudi energy infrastructure.

HEADLINES

Trump Calls Xi Meeting 'Very Productive.' What Investors Might Not Like.

President Donald Trump said Friday he had a "very productive" meeting

with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and that he thought farmers would be

"really happy," but offered few details.

Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a television interview

Friday that details of what the two sides reached on trade would come

Monday.

Investors likely will be pleased to see signs of a fragile peace

between the two economic superpowers-and indications that the leaders

could meet at least twice more this year. But the lack of deals and a

shorter-than-expected extension of the rivals' latest truce leaves plenty

of uncertainty for markets in the months ahead.

Consumer Sentiment Ticked Lower in September

Consumer sentiment declined in September, according to the University

of Michigan's monthly survey, but the mood improved from the survey's

preliminary reading.

The survey's headline index landed at 48.1, versus 47.8 in its initial

September reading published earlier this month. That was still a decline

from August, when the reading was 51.7.

"Overall, interviews reveal broad agreement across the political

spectrum that the outlook for the economy has weakened since the

beginning of the year," the survey's director, Joanne Hsu, said. "After

particularly large declines in sentiment this month, Republican sentiment

is now 20% lower than January 2026; Democrats are down 13% over the same

period," Hsu said.

Durable Goods Orders Were Unchanged in August

Demand for U.S. durable goods was unchanged in August, according to

data published by the Commerce Department.

Total orders for durable goods-which comprise goods meant to last

three years or more-decreased $0.1 billion in August to $338.6 billion,

following a 0.9% July increase.

Economists polled by The Wall Street Journal had expected a decrease

of 0.3%.

Blackstone's Top Private-Equity Executive Is Preparing to Leave Firm

Blackstone's top private-equity executive, Joseph Baratta, is

preparing to leave the firm, according to people familiar with the

matter, the latest in a series of departures by senior leaders from the

private-investment giant.

Baratta, who has been with Blackstone for nearly three decades, has

been the firm's global head of private equity since 2012 and is one of

its most senior executives. He is also a Blackstone board member and part

of the firm's management committee. The exact timing of his departure

hasn't been determined, but it is likely to come around the end of this

year, the people said.

A spokeswoman for Blackstone confirmed Baratta's pending departure.

U.S. Appeals Court Upholds Pentagon Labeling Anthropic a Security Risk

WASHINGTON-A federal appeals court upheld the Defense Department's

decision to designate Anthropic a security risk, giving the Trump

administration a win in its complicated feud with one of the nation's top

artificial-intelligence developers.

The federal appeals court in Washington said in a 2-1 decision Friday

that the law giving the Pentagon the authority to deem a company a

supply-chain risk gave Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth the latitude to

take the action against Anthropic because the company's refusal to have

its AI tools used in mass surveillance or autonomous weapons could

undermine military operations.

"The Department had ample support for its conclusion that the

continued integration of Claude into the Department's information

systems, by the Department or its contractors, presented a statutorily

covered national-security risk," the court wrote.

Cracks in Oracle's AI Data-Center Build-Out Appear in Massive New Mexico

Project

Oracle set out last year to lease a massive AI data-center campus

being built in New Mexico's Doña Ana County, part of a blitz of deals to

create computing power for OpenAI.

The company made aggressive financial commitments for the facility in

contracts that allow it little wiggle room. Now, "Project Jupiter" is

mired in challenges over power supply and permitting and is fast becoming

a prime example of the risks in the tech giant's sprawling and expensive

artificial-intelligence gambit.

Oracle signed a lease for the New Mexico facility with so-called

hell-or-high-water terms, meaning the deal can't be terminated and Oracle

is obligated to make rent payments regardless of whether it has secured

the power to operate the data centers, according to people with knowledge

of the deal.

TALKING POINT AllianceBernstein Names Private Wealth Leader as Next CEO AllianceBernstein President Onur Erzan will succeed longtime CEO Seth Bernstein as chief executive on April 1, the investment management firm said on Friday morning. Bernstein will continue to serve on the company's board of directors.

In picking Erzan, AllianceBernstein is turning to an executive with experience in the wealth and asset management business. Erzan has overseen the company's Bernstein Private Wealth Management unit and striven to expand its offerings for ultrawealthy clients. He also played a key role in helping AllianceBernstein launch actively managed exchange-traded funds, according to the company.

Erzan joined AllianceBernstein in 2021 and assumed the role of president in January 2026, overseeing AllianceBernstein's private wealth management, global private alternatives and global asset management distribution businesses. Before joining AllianceBernstein, he spent 20 years at consulting firm McKinsey & Company, where he was a senior partner and co-leader of its wealth and asset management practice.

AllianceBernstein is a subsidiary of Equitable Holdings and had $919 billion in assets under management as of Aug. 31. Equitable Holdings CEO Mark Pearson cited Erzan's experience as a reason he is the right person for the job. "Since joining AB, he has helped shape the firm's strategy, expand its capabilities and position the business for continued growth," Pearson says.

TD Cowen analyst Bill Katz says the CEO transition appears "orderly." Katz expects greater focus on growing the company's private wealth management business and less chance of a sale to another company. He gives shares of AllianceBernstein a Hold rating.

Shares of AllianceBernstein were down 0.23% late Friday morning. The benchmark S&P 500 index was flat. AllianceBernstein's stock is down 8.19% this year compared with a 13% gain for the S&P 500.

Seth Bernstein will retire as CEO on March 31 after nearly a decade in the role. During his tenure, the company expanded beyond its traditional active public market asset management roots into alternative investments, private wealth, insurance asset management and retirement solutions. He also oversaw the company moving its headquarters to Nashville, Tenn., from New York.

  • Andrew Welsch, Barron's

data.title: RegenLab, Regenerative Medicine Devices and PRP/HA Platforms, Files for Nasdaq IPO
data.description:
RegenLab filed an S‑1 on September 25, 2026 for an underwritten initial public offering. The company plans to list on the Nasdaq under the ticker “RGNA,” with StoneX Financial Inc. as sole book‑running manager. The filing does not yet specify a price range or share count; proceeds are earmarked for sales expansion, manufacturing equipment, R&D and regulatory efforts, and working capital.

Business Description

RegenLab is a regenerative medicine device company that designs and manufactures standardized systems for preparing autologous platelet‑rich plasma (PRP), PRP combined with hyaluronic acid (HA), bone marrow concentrates, and fibrin‑based matrices. Its portfolio spans musculoskeletal regeneration, advanced wound care, medical aesthetics/dermatology, and women’s health, with more than 70 granted patents and approximately 300 clinical studies cited across use cases. The company operates three manufacturing sites in New Jersey (USA), Les Ulis (France), and Monthey (Switzerland), and sells through a mix of direct teams in key countries and a large distributor network.

Flagship products include RegenKit PRP systems (CE‑MDR and multiple FDA 510(k) clearances), Cellular Matrix (PRP+HA; CE‑MDR, PMA in process in the U.S.), and CMS‑reimbursed RegenKit Wound Gel in the U.S. The company reports that RegenKit PRP and Cellular Matrix together contributed about 90% of revenue in 2025. Strategic partnerships include MiMedx (exclusive U.S. distribution for wound gel), Stryker (non‑exclusive U.S. distribution in sports medicine and other fields), OPKO Health Spain (private‑label distribution), and Smith+Nephew (commercial facilitation in Spain).

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Knee osteoarthritis market estimated at approximately $5.9 billion; wound biologics about $8.8 billion in 2022.
  • Market growth: Wound biologics expected ~7.5% CAGR (2022–2026); global PRP preparation kits market projected from ~$756 million (2025) to ~$1.86 billion by 2032 (13.73% CAGR).
  • Market position: Vertically integrated PRP/PRP+HA platform with CE-MDR clearances, FDA clearances for select kits, and CMS-reimbursed wound gel in the U.S.
  • Key competitors: Terumo, Arthrex, Zimmer Biomet, Stryker/Globus-Harvest, EmCyte, DSM Biomedical, Celling Biosciences, BTI (Endoret).
  • Industry trends: Shift toward autologous biologics, combinations of PRP with HA, outpatient wound care solutions, and growing reimbursement frameworks for biologic wound therapies.

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Sold via direct teams in the U.S., Switzerland, France, Germany, Spain and through 120+ distributor agreements globally
  • Locations: Three manufacturing sites (NJ, USA; Les Ulis, France; Monthey, Switzerland)
  • Geographic presence: Commercialized in more than 90 countries
  • Partnerships: MiMedx (U.S. wound care), Stryker (U.S. distribution), OPKO Health Spain (private‑label), Smith+Nephew (Spain facilitation), Leonardino (implants/scaffolds R&D)
  • Other key metrics: ~70 granted patents; ~300 clinical studies cited; ~200 full‑time employees; CMS reimbursement for PRP wound applications (OPPS APC 5054 national rate ~$1,829 in CY2025)

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): $49.17 million (FY2025)
  • Revenue growth: Up 1.6% year over year (2025 vs. 2024)
  • Gross profit: $34.24 million (~69.6% margin)
  • Operating income: $0.68 million
  • Net income: ($1.24 million)

Management

  • Antonino Turzi, Executive Chairman and Chief Executive Officer - Founder; serial life sciences entrepreneur and author of 100+ patents/patent applications.
  • Jean-Marc Biscarrat, Chief Financial Officer and Director - 25+ years in financial leadership roles at public and private companies; led M&A and ERP deployments.
  • Dr. Giuseppe Calloni, PhD, CEO, RegenLab USA LLC - 25 years in executive roles across biotech/chemicals globally; 25 publications, 3 patents, 2 books.
  • Dr. Daphné Metzger, PhD, Chief Operating Officer - Leads global regulatory and GMP operations; oversaw ISO 13485 and MDSAP certifications and site build‑outs.
  • Eric Del Cotto, Independent Director - 25+ years in MedTech/commercial leadership across Europe; market access and growth strategy expertise.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: RegenLab USA, Inc.
  • Filing date: September 25, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: RGNA
  • Exchange: Nasdaq
  • Lead underwriters: StoneX Financial Inc.
  • Use of proceeds: Sales and marketing, factory equipment in France, Switzerland and the U.S., R&D and regulatory expenses for clinical studies in Europe and the U.S., and working capital and general corporate purposes.

Original SEC Filing: Regenlab USA Inc. - S-1 - Sep. 25, 2026

data.title: Jobs report, inflation data to test US rate path, economic strength
data.description:
Key points:
  • September employment report seen showing 100,000 added jobs
  • PCE data on Wednesday set to show inflation trends
  • Rising US bond yields, narrowing market could pose risks to rally

By Lewis Krauskopf

Investors will sift through reports on employment and inflation in the coming week to assess chances of a sharper trajectory of interest rate hikes, which could undermine the US stock market's rally.

Major equity indexes hovered near record levels on Friday, with the S&P 500 less than 1% below its mid-August peak, supported by technology and AI-linked stocks.

The monthly employment report, due on October 2, will be the main event for Wall Street. A key inflation gauge will also be in focus. Investors are scanning for implications for the Federal Reserve, which began raising interest rates this month for the first time in three years to fight high inflation.

"When you step back and you look at what matters to the market right now, the Fed is front and center, interest rates are front and center," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer with Plante Moran Financial Advisors. "Both of those will be pretty important reports as indicators of how Fed thinking might evolve."

TROUBLE FROM BONDS — AND BELOW MARKET'S SURFACE?

Equity indexes were showing resilience despite threats, mainly the continued march higher in Treasury yields, as a selloff extended with investors demanding greater compensation to hold government bonds. The 30-year Treasury yield this week reached its highest level in over 20 years and the benchmark 10-year yield rose well above the closely watched 5% threshold.

"With the action in the fixed-income market over the past several months, it’s not out of the question that things could turn south rather quickly," Matthew Maley, chief market strategist at Miller Tabak, said in a note on Thursday.

Pockets of the stock market have struggled in September, leaving investors wary of broader weakness. The S&P 500, which is more heavily influenced by stocks with the largest market capitalizations, is so far little changed in September, and remained up about 13% in 2026.

But eight of 11 S&P 500 sectors are in negative territory so far for the month, with financials and utilities among those down about 5%. An equal-weight version of the index — which is seen as a barometer for the average stock — was down about 4% in September.

"The averages have held up well, but the average stock has not," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest Wealth Management. "Beneath the surface, there has been some erosion."

The heavyweight tech sector has gained this month, including semiconductor shares, among the biggest winners of the AI trade. Memory chipmaker Micron Technology , whose market value has soared above $1 trillion, is due to report quarterly results on Wednesday.

PAYROLLS LOOM AS RATE-HIKE BETS FIRM

The payrolls report for September is expected to show growth of 100,000 jobs and an unemployment rate of 4.2%, according to a Reuters poll of economists.

"Expectations are that the labor market has improved in recent months," said James Ragan, co-CIO and director of investment management research at D.A. Davidson. "That positive jobs trajectory is important to give confidence that consumer spending is going to stay strong."

A blowout jobs report the prior month solidified expectations the Fed would raise rates. The central bank hiked rates by a quarter percentage point on September 16, and signaled it would raise again before the year is out. Fed Funds futures on Thursday suggested a greater than 60% chance the central bank hikes at its next meeting in October, according to LSEG data.

"The market would be pretty happy with a good but not great payrolls report," Baird said. "If payrolls were to come in exceedingly hot, that could easily elicit a short-term negative market reaction as it would be viewed as further cementing the case for another rate hike in October."

Rate hikes pose several challenges for stocks. They raise borrowing costs and slow the economy while leading to higher bond yields that create more investment competition for stocks.

Wednesday's monthly read of the personal consumption expenditures price index (PCE), closely followed by the Fed, will offer insight into inflation trends. In the prior report, the core PCE index increased 3.3% in the 12 months through July, well above the central bank's 2% target.

The report "will probably confirm that inflation is still running above target," Nolte said. But "if we can see PCE trending a little bit lower, that will give people ... a little more excitement maybe in the market."

data.title: Titan International Files 8K - Entry Into Definitive Agreement >TWI
data.description:
Titan International Inc. (TWI) filed a Form 8K - Entry Into a Definitive Agreement - with the U.S Securities and Exchange Commission on September 25, 2026.

On September 21, 2026, wholly owned subsidiaries Titan ITM Holding S.p.A. and Titan Europe Limited (the "Sellers") of Titan International, Inc., a Delaware corporation (the "Company"), entered into a Sale and Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") to sell all of the outstanding equity interests of Italtractor ITM S.p.A. ("ITM"), a wholly-owned subsidiary of the Company, to USCO S.p.A., a joint stock company incorporated under the laws of Italy ("Purchaser"). Pursuant to the Purchase Agreement, Purchaser will acquire all of the outstanding equity interests of ITM (the "Transaction") for approximately $207 million in cash, plus the opportunity to receive up to an approximately $6 million earnout payment based on ITM's achievement of specified performance criteria for 2026 (the "Purchase Price"). The purchase price is subject to certain adjustments specified in the Purchase Agreement, including for ITM and its subsidiaries' working capital, transaction expenses, cash, and indebtedness as of the closing of the Transaction.

ITM is a global designer, manufacturer and service provider of undercarriage components and complete undercarriage solutions. The business serves original equipment and aftermarket customers across construction, mining, forestry, road-building, agricultural and other specialized applications through an international manufacturing, service and distribution network. ITM includes the following foreign entities: (i) 100% of the corporate capital of Titan Intertractor Gmbh, a company incorporated under the laws of Germany, (ii) 62.5% of the corporate capital of Titan ITM (Tianjin) Ltd, a company incorporated under the laws of the People's Republic of China, (iii) 100% of the corporate capital of Intertractor America Corporation, a company incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware, (iv) 99.03% of the corporate capital of ITM Latin America Industria de Pecas para Tratores Ltda, a company incorporated under the laws of Brazil, (v) 99.885% of the corporate capital of Pyrsa Piezas y Rodajes S.A., a company incorporated under the laws of Spain, (vi) 100% of the corporate capital of ITM Mining Pty Limited, a company incorporated under the laws of Australia, and (vii) 99.978% of the corporate capital of ITM Undercarriage Solutions (India) Private Limited, a company incorporated under the laws of India.

Each party's obligation to consummate the Transaction is subject to certain closing conditions set forth in the Purchase Agreement, including, among others, (i) subject to certain exceptions, the accuracy of the representations and warranties of the other party, (ii) performance in all material respects by the other party of its covenants, (iii) receipt of specified required antitrust and governmental foreign direct investment approvals, (iv) the absence of any law, order or other governmental action prohibiting consummation of the Transaction, and (v) with respect to Purchaser's obligation to close, satisfaction of certain key employee retention conditions and the absence of a continuing material adverse effect with respect to ITM.

The Purchase Agreement also provides that the Sellers will indemnify the Purchaser for losses incurred as a result of breaches of Sellers' representations, warranties, covenants and certain other matters. These indemnification obligations are subject to the limitations set forth in the Purchase Agreement.

The Transaction is currently expected to close in January 2027, subject to the satisfaction or waiver of the applicable closing conditions. Titan currently intends to use a portion of the transaction proceeds to reduce existing debt and strengthen its balance sheet. In future periods, the Company also expects to deploy capital toward key growth investments, including accretive acquisitions and strategic partnerships that expand Titan's capabilities, strengthen its market positions and support the Company's long-term transformation.

The Purchase Agreement contains representations, warranties, covenants, indemnification provisions and termination rights customary for a transaction of this nature. In addition, the parties have agreed to enter into certain transition arrangements at closing, including a transition services agreement under which the Company or one of its affiliates would be expected to provide certain technology, financial and operational transition services to the Purchaser for a certain amount of time following the closing of the Transaction. The Purchase Agreement contains a five-year non-compete covenant restricting the Company from competing in the undercarriage component business in specified jurisdictions with certain exclusions. In addition, the Company has also agreed to certain customer and supplier non-solicit and employee non-hire obligations in specified jurisdictions during the non-compete period.

The Purchase Agreement further provides for the payment of certain termination fees by Purchaser under specified circumstances set forth in the Purchase Agreement, including certain circumstances relating to the failure to obtain required regulatory approvals.

Affiliates of One Equity Partners, a middle market private equity firm, hold a minority ownership interest in the Purchaser. Richard Cashin, the Chairman of One Equity Partners, is a member of the Company's Board of Directors. Mr. Cashin abstained from participating in any deliberations or decisions by the Company's Board of Directors with respect to the proposed Transaction and Purchase Agreement. The Company's Board of Directors and Audit Committee have approved the Transaction and the terms of the Purchase Agreement.

The foregoing description of the Purchase Agreement and the Transaction does not purport to be complete and is qualified in its entirety by reference to the Purchase Agreement, which is filed as Exhibit 2.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K and incorporated herein by reference.

The Purchase Agreement has been included to provide investors and security holders with information regarding its terms. It is not intended to provide any other factual information about the Company, Purchaser, ITM or their respective subsidiaries or affiliates. The representations, warranties and covenants contained in the Purchase Agreement were made only for purposes of the Purchase Agreement and as of specific dates, were solely for the benefit of the parties thereto, may be subject to limitations agreed upon by the contracting parties, including being qualified by confidential disclosures exchanged between the parties in connection with the execution of the Purchase Agreement, and may be subject to standards of materiality applicable to the contracting parties that differ from those applicable to investors. Investors should not rely on the representations, warranties or covenants as characterizations of the actual state of facts or condition of the Company, Purchaser, ITM or their respective subsidiaries or affiliates. Moreover, information concerning the subject matter of the representations, warranties and covenants may change after the date of the Purchase Agreement, which subsequent information may or may not be fully reflected in the Company's public disclosures.

data.title: Liberty Global shortlists bidders for Belgian fiber stake - Bloomberg
data.description:
Liberty Global chose three bidders to move to next round of bidding for a stake in Belgian network firm Wyre.

French infrastructure fund Ardian, French fund InfraVia Capital Partners SAS and Canada’s Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan were selected to move on, according to a Bloomberg report  on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Deliberations are ongoing and details such as size and timing of the deal may change, according to the report.. Representatives for Liberty Global, Ardian, InfraVia and OTPP declined to comment to Bloomberg.

Bloomberg reported in April  that Liberty Global was working with Goldman Sachs on the sale and the stake in Wyre could be worth about €1 billion ($1.1 billion).
